availability_note: Same Sootopolis party (Rillaboom 36, Kartana 20, Flutter Mane 68, Incineroar 36, Raging Bolt 60, Zapdos 30 reachable legend); Sootopolis after the cavern and Cave of Origin, Rain Badge not earned, nothing from Ever Grande or the League. Only the two Grass leads were used.

attempts.note: I deliberately let Lumineon (faster than Rillaboom) act on T1 to see the Surf tactic: it Protected instead while Gastrodon chose Surf (the mirror direction of the tactic) and died to a 4x Leaf Blade first. T2 Leaf Blade took Lumineon (after it set Tailwind) and Wood Hammer took Seaking. T3 Huntail Shell Smashed (White Herb repaired) and died to Wood Hammer; Octillery Protected. T4 Grassy Glide took Octillery and a +2 Leaf Blade took Starmie after its Ice Beam broke Kartana's Sash (219).

strategy_checks.check: Authored tactic: Lumineon Surf into the board so Gastrodon's Storm Drain grows
strategy_checks.evidence: T1 Lumineon chose Protect while Gastrodon (the intended receiver) chose Surf - the AI ran the engine backwards (Gastrodon Surf would have fed Lumineon's Storm Drain instead) and neither resolved because Gastrodon was OHKOed first. Against a double-Grass lead, Surf into two resists is also a poor click, so the tactic being skipped is defensible; the receiver-side Surf pick is the odd part.

T3 Protect (blocked a 2x Leaf Blade), T4 OHKOed by priority Grassy Glide before moving.

protect_ledger.payoff: REAL - blocked Wood Hammer; but it spent the tactic turn, and Gastrodon died beside it.
REAL - blocked a lethal Leaf Blade; Huntail Smashed beside it and died anyway.

ai_defects.board: Gastrodon + Lumineon vs Rillaboom + Kartana (both Grass)
ai_defects.better: The authored tactic is Lumineon Surf -> Gastrodon; the AI selected the reverse (receiver Surfs, setter Protects). With two Grass foes the right click was Gastrodon Ice Beam / Lumineon Icy Wind or Tailwind; Surf into a double Grass board is the worst option. Tactic wiring worth checking: it may be firing on the wrong battler.

authored_set_legality: No problem found. Levels L84 x5, Starmie L85.
theme_note: No - the redirection lesson never appeared, because the crack line (Grass ignores the matrix) is exactly what a player brings to a Water gym, and the engine's two bodies died on turns 1 and 2. The room reads as six Waters that fold to Grass; the clever part is only visible if the player leads something else.
